questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL partial index covers rows where `x < 2`. A generic prepared query filters `x < $1`, with arbitrary parameter values. Why can that index fail to be usable?

choices.text: Prepared queries cannot use partial indexes.
The predicate is not implied for every parameter value.
The index stores rows with x greater than 2 after preparation completes.
PostgreSQL must execute every partial-index query as a sequential scan.

questions.explanation: The planner must prove predicate implication at planning time. x < $1 does not imply x < 2 for every possible value; this is not a blanket ban on prepared queries.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 11.8. Partial Indexes
sources.claim: A partial index can be used only when the planner can prove the query condition implies its predicate; parameterized conditions generally cannot establish that implication.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL index stores `lower(email)`. During an indexed lookup using that expression, where is the indexed expression value obtained?

choices.text: By recomputing it for every table row.
From a separate generated SQL function created for each lookup request.
From the stored index entry.
By changing the stored email column permanently to lowercase first.

questions.explanation: Expression index entries hold the computed result. This speeds suitable searches but shifts computation and maintenance cost to writes.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 11.7. Indexes on Expressions
sources.claim: Expression indexes store computed values and incur expression computation at inserts and non-HOT updates; lookups use stored index values.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL migration uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on a busy table. Which constraints or failure modes matter? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A build failure always removes every trace of the index automatically.
It cannot run inside a transaction block.
A failed build can leave an invalid index behind.
It performs more work than an ordinary index build.
CONCURRENTLY guarantees the build never waits for other transactions.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: an invalid catalog index can remain after failure. B is correct: concurrent index creation has transaction-management restrictions. C is correct: the invalid index may need to be dropped and rebuilt. D is correct: multiple scans and transaction waits add overhead. E is incorrect: it can wait for transactions and snapshots at documented stages.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: CREATE INDEX
sources.claim: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY performs multiple scans, cannot run in a transaction block, and can leave an invalid index after failure.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL partial index includes only unbilled orders. A query does not restrict billing status. Why can that index not by itself answer the complete query?

choices.text: Its rows are invisible to SELECT.
The query must first turn the partial index into an ordinary full index.
Partial indexes cannot store the same column values as full indexes.
It omits rows the query may need.

questions.explanation: A partial index contains a subset. Queries must imply its predicate before the planner can rely on it for a complete answer.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 11.8. Partial Indexes
sources.claim: A partial index can be used only when the planner can prove the query condition implies its predicate; parameterized conditions generally cannot establish that implication.

questions.prompt: A write-heavy PostgreSQL table adds several expression indexes. Which cost should its owner include in the write path?

choices.text: Computing and maintaining index expressions.
Re-running all SELECT queries before commit.
Converting all indexed expressions into stored table columns automatically.
Disabling all index maintenance until the next server-wide checkpoint.

questions.explanation: Expression indexes calculate expressions on insert and non-HOT updates and maintain their index entries. They are not free computed lookup metadata.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 11.7. Indexes on Expressions
sources.claim: Expression indexes store computed values and incur expression computation at inserts and non-HOT updates; lookups use stored index values.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL concurrent index build fails during a production migration. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An invalid index can still impose update overhead.
Wrapping a concurrent rebuild in BEGIN makes its multi-scan work atomic.
Two concurrent index builds may run on the same table simultaneously without restriction.
CONCURRENTLY means every table write is blocked for the entire build.
An invalid index is ignored for query planning.

questions.explanation: A is correct: its maintenance can consume write work despite being unusable for queries. B is incorrect: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. C is incorrect: only one concurrent index build on a table can run at a time. D is incorrect: its purpose is to avoid the ordinary build lock that prevents writes, though other waits remain. E is correct: the planner cannot use an invalid index as a usable access path.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: CREATE INDEX
sources.claim: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY performs multiple scans, cannot run in a transaction block, and can leave an invalid index after failure.
